message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Home Depot's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-01-28) and checked the live quote, which showed HD at $385.43 (bid $385.41 / ask $385.45). The fundamentals support a modest starter position: fiscal 2023 net sales of $152,669M, operating income of $21,689M, net income of $15,143M, diluted EPS of $15.11, and operating cash flow of $21,172M — a still very profitable, cash-generative business, even though sales and operating income slipped from fiscal 2022 ($157,403M and $24,039M), which is why I sized the position conservatively rather than aggressively. One important note: the 10-K text returned by the filing tool stated net income of $18,470M and diluted EPS of $18.42, which conflicts with the trusted SEC-filed figures of $15,143M and $15.11; I relied on the trusted lookup values and flagged the discrepancy rather than acting on the inconsistent numbers. I placed a single buy limit order for 12 shares of HD at $385.45 (the current ask), which filled at $385.45 for roughly $4,625 — within the $5,000 per-order cap, within the $10,000 daily total, buy-side only, and with a limit price at the market. No cash was withdrawn from the account, and the only other holding remains the pre-existing 50 NVDA shares.
